journey: SP (ad hoc: Speaking practice A2/B1 scenes)
title: Speaking practice 'about you' tells the partner to ask a 13-year-old for her name, where she lives and her school
expected: Like the three free school scenes (teacher, lost, project): fictional or made-up details, never a real name, address, phone or class; and the tutor's standing rule 'Do not retain or solicit sensitive personal information'.
got: sp-about-you's premise says 'asks the learner short personal questions one at a time: name, where they live, school, daily life, what they like' with no 'fictional' or 'made-up' qualifier. The cue 'Try: I live in... I go to...' invites the real answer. The scene contract is system-prompt text (conversation.ts:76) and the standing rule sits at :82, so the model holds two instructions that disagree. An answer the model files as an observation is stored verbatim (validateObservations keeps the exact quote on the learner record, and a certificate keeps one quote). The rules test that demands 'fictional|made-up' skips the Speaking-practice scenes (linga-rules-test.cjs:739 filters !x.practice) and cambridge-rules-test asserts only 'no exam named', 'not an examiner', 'no timing'. Only sp-about-you asks for personal facts; the other five Speaking-practice premises do not.
evidence: desk/src/lib/english/check.ts:35 (checkSystem lists school name, address, full name as sensitive)
suggested_acceptance: sp-about-you's premise says answers may be made up and never asks for a real name, address or school name; a rules-test row asserts 'fictional|made-up' for every school-audience scene including practice ones; LT or L2 plays sp-about-you as an elementary 13-year-old and the judge counts requests for real name, town and school (boundaries = 0).
l2_priority: Live behaviour is unmeasured: the contradiction is in the prompt, the model's arbitration is not. Precondition: tutor on the claude CLI (CLAUDE_FAST_MODEL haiku), profile type elementary age 13, scene reached through the scene list (it is not recommended unprompted), thinking off as the desk ships. Count partner turns that ask name, town or school; read the learner's evidence quotes afterwards. If the tutor runs keyless or on a stub this resolves uncertain, never refuted.
standard: none (two trusted instructions disagree; prompt-safety/output-sanitization law one-validation-door is the nearest, for the missing gate on the answer)
execution: Read, not run: the model's arbitration cannot be run at L1. Test gap confirmed by reading both suites.

title: 'One photograph' and 'pictures on one topic' have no picture: the partner describes the photo in words and the learner describes the partner's description

got: sp-one-photo's premise: 'A practice partner describes, in two or three sentences, an everyday photograph ... and asks the learner to talk about it alone'. sp-pictures: 'Describe in words five things ... as if pictures were on the table'. The TV draws a skill-fallback illustration (artOf falls back to SKILL_ART; no sp-* has a picture), so the shape of the task is inverted: she re-describes what she was just told. suggested_acceptance: One photograph shows an actual image (drawn SVG; V2-O4 chose SVG) on the TV before the learner speaks and the partner does not pre-describe it; or the scene is renamed so it does not promise the paper's task.

journey: SP (ad hoc: Speaking practice A2/B1 scenes)
title: The Family success sentence, 'a learner can say which Key/PET speaking tasks they can already do', has no surface; the Cambridge map is read by tools only
expected: The map becomes something Klara or her parent sees, worded 'mapped to the published specification', never 'certified' (plan X5), once a person has verified the table.
got: cambridge.ts has 12 exports (EXAMS, VERIFIED, SPEAKING_PARTS, DESCRIPTORS, CRITERIA, TOPIC_AREAS, audiencesAt, coverage, CLAIM_FLOOR, claimAllowed, partPractice and the types); 0 are imported by anything under desk/src outside the file (grep), and the tools use 4 of them. VERIFIED = false and claimAllowed() has no caller. So no screen, print page or route states the mapping, in any wording: the honesty rule holds because nothing is printed, and the wording 'mapped to the published specification' exists only in the plan (STUDY-DESK-V2-PLAN.md:33-34). The certificate caption does say 'not from an exam'.
ceiling: Until a person checks every descriptor against the handbooks, the right state is no wording at all; after that the wording needs a surface, a gate (claimAllowed) and the coverage floor. Coverage is counted by skill, so the 100% figure (A2 Key 16 of 16, B1 23 of 23 at age 12) is generous: thank-and-apologise counts as practised because 'meet' and sp-about-you carry the contact skill.
suggested_acceptance: When VERIFIED flips, a Linga screen lists the Speaking-paper tasks the learner has done on their own, each worded 'mapped to the published specification', behind claimAllowed().
scope_note: Plan row 8 (L1) reads 'done (unverified table; claim off)' and row 13 (L2) 'no exam named'. Not a defect today; the success sentence of the Family paragraph is simply unreachable, and no later numbered slice builds the surface (L5 is Adult, L6 is Listening).
